subject: Green Iguana
fact: Green iguanas are strong climbers and have long tails that help with balance.

subject: Marine Iguana
fact: Marine iguanas are the only modern lizards that regularly feed in the ocean.

subject: Veiled Chameleon
fact: Chameleons can move their eyes independently and shoot out long sticky tongues.

subject: Panther Chameleon
fact: Panther chameleons can display many bright color patterns.

subject: Bearded Dragon
fact: Bearded dragons can puff up the spiny skin under their throats.

subject: Komodo Dragon
fact: Komodo dragons are the largest living lizards.

subject: Gila Monster
fact: Gila monsters are venomous lizards that store fat in their thick tails.

subject: Leopard Gecko
fact: Leopard geckos have movable eyelids and can shed their tails to escape danger.

subject: Crested Gecko
fact: Crested geckos have ridges above their eyes that look like tiny eyelashes.

subject: Tokay Gecko
fact: Tokay geckos are large colorful geckos known for loud calls.

subject: Blue-Tongued Skink
fact: Blue-tongued skinks flash their bright blue tongues when threatened.

subject: Green Anole
fact: Green anoles can change between green and brown shades.

subject: Frilled Lizard
fact: Frilled lizards can spread a large skin frill around their necks.

subject: Common Basilisk
fact: Basilisk lizards can sprint across the surface of water for short distances.

subject: Thorny Devil
fact: Thorny devils are covered in spikes and collect moisture between the scales of their skin.

subject: Nile Monitor
fact: Monitor lizards are active hunters with long necks, strong tails, and forked tongues.

subject: Corn Snake
fact: Corn snakes are nonvenomous snakes that kill prey by constriction.

subject: Ball Python
fact: Ball pythons may curl into a tight ball when frightened.

subject: King Cobra
fact: King cobras are the longest venomous snakes in the world.

subject: Western Diamondback Rattlesnake
fact: Rattlesnakes shake special tail segments to make a warning buzz.

subject: Boa Constrictor
fact: Boa constrictors wrap their muscular bodies around prey.

subject: Green Anaconda
fact: Green anacondas are among the heaviest snakes in the world.

subject: Garter Snake
fact: Garter snakes are widespread snakes that often live near gardens and wetlands.

subject: Milk Snake
fact: Milk snakes are nonvenomous and often have bold bands of red, black, and pale colors.

subject: Hognose Snake
fact: Hognose snakes have upturned snouts that help them dig in loose soil.

subject: Black Mamba
fact: Black mambas are fast venomous snakes native to parts of Africa.

subject: Reticulated Python
fact: Reticulated pythons are among the longest snakes in the world.

subject: Yellow-Bellied Sea Snake
fact: Sea snakes have flattened tails that help them swim.

subject: Nile Crocodile
fact: Nile crocodiles are powerful predators that live in African rivers and lakes.

subject: American Alligator
fact: American alligators build nests from plants and mud.

subject: Gharial
fact: Gharials have very long narrow snouts adapted for catching fish.

subject: Spectacled Caiman
fact: Spectacled caimans get their name from a raised ridge between their eyes.

subject: Green Sea Turtle
fact: Green sea turtles migrate long distances between feeding and nesting areas.

subject: Loggerhead Sea Turtle
fact: Loggerheads have large heads and strong jaws that can crush hard-shelled prey.

subject: Leatherback Sea Turtle
fact: Leatherbacks are the largest sea turtles and have flexible leathery shells.

subject: Red-Eared Slider
fact: Red-eared sliders are named for the red patches behind their eyes.

subject: Eastern Box Turtle
fact: Box turtles can close their hinged lower shells tightly for protection.

subject: Common Snapping Turtle
fact: Snapping turtles have strong jaws and long tails.

subject: Galápagos Tortoise
fact: Galápagos tortoises can live for well over a century.

subject: African Spurred Tortoise
fact: African spurred tortoises are large desert tortoises that dig deep burrows.

subject: Poison Dart Frog
fact: Some poison dart frogs get defensive chemicals from the foods they eat in the wild.

subject: Green Tree Frog
fact: Tree frogs have toe pads that help them cling to leaves and branches.

subject: American Bullfrog
fact: Bullfrogs are large frogs with deep calls that can carry across ponds.

subject: Glass Frog
fact: Many glass frogs have partly transparent skin on their undersides.

subject: Red-Eyed Tree Frog
fact: Red-eyed tree frogs have bright red eyes and sticky toe pads.

subject: Tomato Frog
fact: Tomato frogs can puff up their round bodies when threatened.

subject: Horned Frog
fact: Horned frogs have wide mouths and sit quietly while waiting for prey.

subject: Northern Leopard Frog
fact: Leopard frogs are named for the dark spots across their backs and legs.

subject: American Toad
fact: Toads have bumpy skin and produce defensive chemicals from glands behind their eyes.

subject: Cane Toad
fact: Cane toads are large toads with strong defensive glands.

subject: Fire-Bellied Toad
fact: Fire-bellied toads show bright belly colors as a warning to predators.

subject: Axolotl
fact: Axolotls keep their feathery external gills as adults.

subject: Tiger Salamander
fact: Tiger salamanders spend much of their lives hidden underground.

subject: Fire Salamander
fact: Fire salamanders have striking yellow markings on dark skin.

subject: Eastern Newt
fact: Eastern newts have a bright orange juvenile stage called a red eft.

subject: Olm
fact: Olms are pale cave-dwelling amphibians that can live in complete darkness.

subject: Mudpuppy
fact: Mudpuppies are aquatic salamanders that keep external gills throughout life.

subject: Caecilian
fact: Caecilians are limbless amphibians that look a little like large worms.

subject: Greater Siren
fact: Sirens are eel-shaped amphibians with tiny front legs and no hind legs.

subject: Hellbender
fact: Hellbenders are giant aquatic salamanders that hide beneath rocks in cool streams.
